help_topics.title: Understanding print selection and wave reprint context
help_topics.business_question: Does a returned document selection prove that a document printed?
help_topics.plain_answer: Print selection returns entity context, eligible document definitions and user printer defaults. Wave reprint procedures also return context.
input_context: internalNum int, printProcess int, culture nvarchar(10), username nvarchar(30), all required. No defaults; culture unused.
internalLaunchNum numeric(9), culture nvarchar(10), required; culture unused. No defaults.
internalLaunchNum numeric(9), culture nvarchar(10), required; culture unused. No defaults.
internalLaunchNum numeric(9), culture nvarchar(10), required; culture unused. No defaults.
culture nvarchar(10), required; not referenced. No defaults.

execution_steps.explanation: Read the selected user printer defaults and entity context for the print-process code.
Match eligible DOCUMENT_TYPE slots and default flags, then apply the captured feature-dependent exclusion.
Hand the selection to the configured application/renderer; confirm completion separately.

configuration_dependencies: Match the print-process code and entity ID with the user profile and document process/default pairs.
Printer selection requires CLOSED N; the two reprint context getters do not.
Manifest-close context returns flags only.
boundaries: An unsupported process can change result-set count. Feature/document selector labels remain opaque in the public copy.

cases.question: An unsupported print process was submitted. Are two result sets guaranteed?
must_explain: Only supported branches emit context; the document query still runs.

cases.question: A closed wave appears in reprint context but not printer selection. Is that impossible?
must_explain: Printer selection alone has CLOSED N; reprint getters do not.
must_not_claim: All three getters have the same wave filter.

cases.question: The document appears in a selection. Did the printer receive it?
must_explain: Selection is separate from renderer and printer acknowledgment.

help_topics.title: Finding stored labels and label-print parameters
help_topics.business_question: Why can label lookup return NULL or an unexpected container?
help_topics.plain_answer: The label-image helper retrieves both ordinary and return-label images for an internal container number; DOCUMENT_TYPE does not filter them. The separate print-parameter helper looks up a text container ID without applying its Warehouse argument.
input_context: INTERNAL_CONTAINER_NUM numeric(9), DOCUMENT_TYPE nvarchar(25), required; DOCUMENT_TYPE unused. No defaults.
ContainerID nvarchar(25), Warehouse nvarchar(25), required; Warehouse unused. No defaults.

execution_steps.explanation: Identify whether the request is for stored binary images or print parameters.
Image lookup selects returns flag Y and ordinary flag N; parameter lookup uses text container ID and fixed document/process selectors.
Inspect missing or ambiguous matches before attributing the result to a printer.

configuration_dependencies: Multiple matching images or container IDs are assigned without a defined order.
expected_results: One result row can contain NULL values; no label is printed.

cases.question: Does DOCUMENT_TYPE filter GetShippingLabelImage?
must_explain: The parameter is unused.

cases.question: Does missing image return no result row?
must_explain: The image getter returns one row with NULL image values.

cases.question: Can Warehouse disambiguate duplicate text container IDs in the parameter helper?
must_explain: Warehouse is unused by that body.

help_topics.title: Understanding queued reprint requests
help_topics.business_question: What does the custom reprint procedure actually complete?
help_topics.plain_answer: The reprint routine selects non-NULL container IDs in the specified wave at status 300 and queues Ready DIF messages.
input_context: INTERNAL nvarchar(max), username nvarchar(200), error nvarchar(2000) OUTPUT, success nvarchar(2000) OUTPUT; all required, no defaults. username/error/success are not used or assigned.

execution_steps.explanation: Select qualifying container IDs through a cursor.
Concatenate each ID into a fixed message envelope and insert a Ready DIF request.
Require downstream processing and printer evidence to establish completion.

configuration_dependencies: Routing constants and the business meaning of status 300 depend on deployment configuration.
expected_results: The success and error output parameters are not assigned.
boundaries: There is no deduplication check; rerunning can enqueue the same request again. Earlier messages can remain after a partial failure.
The interpolated container ID is not wrapped in an escaping function.

cases.question: Does Ready prove the label printed?
must_explain: Ready is the inserted request state; downstream completion is unverified.

cases.question: Will a rerun skip already queued containers?
must_explain: No deduplication check is present.

cases.question: Can I trust the success output as a result?
must_explain: The body never assigns that output.
must_not_claim: A populated success result is guaranteed.

help_topics.title: Understanding QC settings versus QC execution
help_topics.business_question: Does loading QC context grant or execute a QC action?
help_topics.plain_answer: The context routine combines user packing-preference flags, system configuration and security checkpoint values into three result sets. It does not inspect containers, assign QC, force a pass or enforce an action itself.
input_context: username nvarchar(30), culture nvarchar(200), warehouse nvarchar(25), all required. No defaults.

execution_steps.explanation: Resolve the existing user packing preference and its NULL fallback.
Read checkpoint values for menu 4005 and relevant action IDs.
Return scalar options and two lookup lists; leave action enforcement to the consuming application.

configuration_dependencies: Missing user is different from existing user with a NULL preference.
No ACTIVE packing-preference filter is applied.
Warehouse is passed through rather than filtering configuration.

cases.question: Does a missing user get the default packing preference?
must_explain: The fallback is inside the existing-user scalar subquery; missing user can leave no preference match.
must_not_claim: Missing and NULL preference are equivalent.

cases.question: Does the routine force a pass when ForceQcPassSec is true?
must_explain: It returns a checkpoint value; it performs no QC mutation.

cases.question: Are these settings confirmed for the current warehouse?
must_explain: No live settings were read and warehouse does not filter the config reads.

help_topics.business_question: Why might a carrier or carrier group be absent from these lookups?
help_topics.plain_answer: Carrier and group lookups return an exact active carrier/service combination or an exact active group.
input_context: Carrier nvarchar(25), CarrierService nvarchar(50), required. No defaults.

execution_steps.explanation: Match the requested carrier/service or group identity.
Require the captured active Y flag.

configuration_dependencies: A NULL carrier service matches only a NULL service; names are exact selectors.

cases.question: Does NULL service mean all services?
must_explain: It explicitly matches a NULL stored service.

cases.question: Does an active record prove a shipment may use the carrier?
must_explain: Rating, calendars, routing and authorization are outside these getters.

cases.question: Does the group getter rate all group members?
must_explain: It reads an active group header only.

cases.question: Will ShipmentSelection return only the chosen internal shipment?
must_explain: It can return all same-ID same-warehouse rows.
must_not_claim: Exactly one chosen shipment is guaranteed.

cases.question: Does MetaTrans_SplitShipment split data?

help_topics.title: Understanding X-of-Y container numbering
help_topics.business_question: Which containers receive X-of-Y numbers, and is wave numbering atomic?
help_topics.plain_answer: Shipment numbering assigns ordinals to identified top-level tree roots and resets identified immediate children to zero. Wave numbering invokes that helper inside one transaction per shipment; the body does not provide one whole-wave transaction.
input_context: internalShipmentNumber numeric(9), required. No default.
waveNumber numeric(9), required. No default.

execution_steps.explanation: Capture qualifying shipment roots using NOLOCK and order by internal ID.
Assign root ordinal/total and reset identified immediate children.
For a wave, capture shipments and invoke the helper in separate BEGIN/COMMIT pairs.

configuration_dependencies: Unidentified or deeper descendant rows are outside the explicit child-reset set.
Ambient caller transactions alter persistence of nested COMMITs.
Both helper membership reads and wave selection use NOLOCK.
expected_results: Stored count fields change; they do not count shipped item quantity.

cases.question: Are all nested descendants reset?
must_explain: Only identified immediate children of selected roots are reset.

cases.question: Does one failed shipment roll back the entire wave automatically?
must_explain: The body has per-shipment transaction pairs and no whole-wave rollback handler.

cases.question: Does COMMIT inside an existing caller transaction persist each shipment?
must_explain: Nested COMMIT does not independently persist an ambient outer transaction.
must_not_claim: Each shipment is independently committed regardless of caller.

help_topics.title: Understanding container counts, location and status flow
help_topics.business_question: Can these helper results prove a uniform container hierarchy?
help_topics.plain_answer: The helpers answer different questions: a row count over selected immediate contents, one distinct location under a branch-specific scope, and one unordered non-NULL status flow from a recursive subtree. None alone proves every descendant is consistent.
input_context: internalcontainernum numeric(9), required. No default.
internalcontainernum numeric(9), required. No default.
internalContainerNum numeric(9), required. No default.

execution_steps.explanation: Distinguish row count from item quantities and distinct items.
Determine whether the location helper uses tree-unit rows or its direct-child fallback.
Treat a returned status flow as one candidate, not unanimous subtree agreement.

configuration_dependencies: Location fallback applies ITEM IS NOT NULL only to its self-row arm.
A NULL location group can contribute to the multiple-location result.
Status-flow TOP 1 has no precedence or explicit recursion override.
expected_results: Count, location-or-NULL and zero/one flow result are separate contracts.

cases.question: Does content count sum quantity?
must_explain: It is COUNT(*) over the documented row predicate.

cases.question: Do all fallback location rows require ITEM?
must_explain: The item predicate applies only to the self-row arm due to AND/OR binding.

cases.question: Does one flow result prove all descendants use it?
must_explain: TOP 1 is unordered and does not enforce agreement.

help_topics.title: Understanding shipping group and transfer mutations
help_topics.business_question: What related records do the group and transfer helpers actually update?
help_topics.plain_answer: These helpers have narrow and different scopes: one moves below-threshold container IDs, one transfers a detail and comments, one updates group/spot and optional names, and one clears work-linked groups. Caller orchestration must coordinate broader shipment consistency.
input_context: fromShipmentInternalNum numeric(9), status numeric(9), toShipmentInternalNum numeric(9), userName nvarchar(30), required. No defaults.
intLineNum numeric(9), destIntShipNum numeric(9), destShipId nvarchar(25), shipTo nvarchar(25), required. No defaults.
renameContainer bit, assignSpot bit, groupNum nvarchar(50), contId nvarchar(25), internalContNum numeric(9), spotNumber numeric(9), required. No defaults.
containerId nvarchar(25), warehouse nvarchar(25), user nvarchar(30), required. No defaults.

execution_steps.explanation: Inspect the captured row selector and whether it is rechecked at mutation time.
Apply only the documented container, detail/comment or work-group changes.
Check broader line, allocation, header and hierarchy consistency in caller logic.

configuration_dependencies: Container move captures status eligibility once.
Group spot MAX+1 lacks a serialization protocol.
Remove-group work joins do not repeat a warehouse restriction on every group member.

cases.question: Does moving containers also move their shipment detail?
must_explain: The move helper updates only container shipment number/stamps.
must_not_claim: It performs the full shipment transfer.

cases.question: Is MAX+1 spot assignment concurrency-safe by itself?
must_explain: No serializable locking or uniqueness protocol is shown.

cases.question: Does detail transfer preserve mark-for contacts?
must_explain: The enumerated MARK_FOR fields are cleared.

help_topics.title: Understanding split quantity boundaries and output IDs
help_topics.business_question: Do shipping split helpers reject quantities larger than the source?
help_topics.plain_answer: Both split helpers reject NULL or nonpositive inputs, but neither completely enforces an upper quantity bound. The allocation helper leaves requested quantity on the original and remainder on the clone; the container helper leaves remainder on the original and requested quantity on the clone.
input_context: qty numeric(19,5), allocReqNum numeric(9), userName nvarchar(30), newAllocReqNum numeric(9) OUTPUT, required. No defaults.
qty numeric(19,5), internalContNum numeric(9), userName nvarchar(30), newInternalContNum numeric(9) OUTPUT, newParentContNum numeric(9) OUTPUT, all required; no defaults.

execution_steps.explanation: Validate source existence, positive quantity and upper bound in the caller before invoking mutation.
Observe each helper cloning and scaling its documented original/clone quantities.
Coordinate the work inside an appropriate caller transaction and handle returned IDs/errors without assuming outputs were cleared.

configuration_dependencies: Missing source is not rejected by a row-count check.
Zero source quantities can cause division by zero.
Container parent output is assigned only in the optional parent branch.
expected_results: A bounded split storage operation whose safe composition depends on caller validation.

cases.question: Is qty greater than source rejected immediately?
must_explain: No complete upper-bound guard exists; one update may be skipped while another proceeds.
must_not_claim: Oversized requests safely fail before changes.

cases.question: Which allocation row retains the requested quantity?
must_explain: The original allocation request retains qty; clone is reduced to remainder.
must_not_claim: The clone always receives requested qty.

cases.question: Can I assume newParentContNum is reset when no parent was created?
must_explain: It is not assigned in the skipped parent branch.
must_not_claim: All outputs are cleared on every path.

help_topics.title: Understanding deallocation output mode and history
help_topics.business_question: Is deallocation outputMode=1 a read-only preview?
help_topics.plain_answer: Deallocation changes inventory in both direction branches. outputMode selects whether the procedure returns captured before-state and allocation data or writes history; it does not select a preview mode.
input_context: waveNum numeric(9), internalShipmentNum numeric(9), direction char(4), invTrack nchar(1), userName nvarchar(30), processStamp nvarchar(100), required; outputMode tinyint defaults to 0.

execution_steps.explanation: Select requests through the OR of nonzero wave and shipment selectors.
Deduct source allocated quantity or destination in-transit quantity and capture before/after inventory.
Choose output rows without history for mode 1, or insert calculated per-shipment history for other modes.

configuration_dependencies: Both zero selectors select nothing; two supplied nonzero selectors broaden selection by OR.
Source matching includes logistics unit/attribute identity; destination matching does not.
History expiry/status calculations do not update those fields in inventory.
boundaries: The procedure sets XACT_ABORT and rethrows errors but begins no transaction.

cases.question: Can outputMode=1 be used as a harmless preview?
must_explain: The inventory UPDATE occurs before the result rows.

cases.question: Does XACT_ABORT create an atomic inventory/history transaction?
must_explain: The body has no BEGIN TRAN; caller transaction ownership is separate.
must_not_claim: XACT_ABORT alone makes the whole body atomic.

cases.question: Are source and destination identity matches identical?
must_explain: Destination omits logistics-unit and attribute identity comparisons used by source.
must_not_claim: Both branches match the same full identity.

help_topics.title: Understanding header freight rollups
help_topics.business_question: Why can recalculated shipment freight be NULL?
help_topics.plain_answer: The routine sums four stored charge fields from selected manifest-state containers with a text parent-container test, then replaces header values. It makes no carrier-rating request. SQL SUM can return NULL when no eligible amounts exist; the body does not turn that into zero.
input_context: internalShipNum numeric(9), required. No default.

execution_steps.explanation: Select shipment containers by captured manifest states and parent-text-ID rule.
Sum total/base freight, discount and accessorial amount.
Replace header amounts with the aggregate variables.

configuration_dependencies: Container eligibility uses the manifest-state constants in the routine and PARENT_CONTAINER_ID text rather than tree-root metadata.

cases.question: Does no eligible container yield zero freight?
must_explain: SUM yields NULL unless non-NULL amounts contribute.

cases.question: Does this call a carrier to rate the shipment?
must_explain: It aggregates stored container charge columns.

cases.question: Does it select only TREE_UNIT roots?
must_explain: It uses a text parent-ID condition, not TREE_UNIT.
must_not_claim: The filter is a tree-root test.

help_topics.business_question: Do interface configuration getters execute configured steps in order?

Apply exact predicates or the prefix LIKE pattern.

must_explain: Neither reviewed flow-step getter has ORDER BY.

cases.question: Does prefix percent mean a literal percent?
must_explain: Prefix participates in LIKE and is not escaped.

cases.question: Does retrieving interface detail prove it is active?
must_explain: The getters do not filter ACTIVE.
must_not_claim: Only active definitions can be returned.

help_topics.title: Understanding upload claims and serial staging
help_topics.business_question: Does claiming an upload batch prove exclusive processing or successful delivery?
help_topics.plain_answer: The batch routine updates header and linked child staging conditions and process stamps. Its claim branch can restamp rows already In Process, and downstream child scope follows the batch stamp. The serial helper inserts selected payload rows without an explicit rerun deduplication check.
input_context: BatchId nvarchar(100), InterfaceDtlKey numeric(9), InterfaceConst nvarchar(25), required. No defaults.
PROCESSSTAMP nvarchar(100), INTERFACEACTIONCODE nvarchar(25), INTERFACECONDITION nvarchar(25), required. No defaults.

execution_steps.explanation: Claim matching-detail non-Processed headers or advance matching-detail In Process headers.
Update linked child records using batch-stamped parent/link selections.
Create selected serial payload rows; rely on separately evidenced transport/acknowledgment for delivery completion.

configuration_dependencies: BatchId reuse can broaden child selection.
NULL interface conditions fail equality/inequality filters.
Claim result uses unordered TOP 1; later result returns all batch-stamped headers.

cases.question: Does In Process prevent a second claimant?
must_explain: Claim excludes Processed, not already In Process; no atomic claim protocol is shown.

cases.question: Are all child updates limited to InterfaceDtlKey?
must_explain: Child selections use batch-stamped linked parents without repeating that key.
must_not_claim: The detail key is applied to every child scope.

cases.question: Will the serial helper skip records from a previous run?
must_explain: There is no anti-join against existing uploads.

help_topics.title: Understanding interface cleanup differences
help_topics.business_question: Are similarly named cleanup procedures interchangeable?
help_topics.plain_answer: Interface cleanup differs by routine: order cleanup 01 selects Processed rows and includes VAS activity; cleanup 02 ignores condition and omits VAS. Receipt cleanup deletes purchase-order header before detail.

must_explain: Its body contains no VAS DELETE.

cases.question: Does upload cleanup remove serials/comments/containers too?
must_explain: It explicitly deletes linked details and headers only.
must_not_claim: It removes the entire upload tree.

help_topics.title: Understanding interface error and retained-data views

must_explain: UNION removes duplicate projected rows.

cases.question: Does the error view send notifications?
must_explain: It projects EMAIL_SENT and other stored fields only.

cases.question: Is a retained-view row proof the latest upload succeeded?
must_explain: No condition or freshness check establishes delivery.
